review_comments.body: ⚠️ Quality: Dropping the if not filter_pattern guard breaks basedpyright CI `filter_pattern_enabled()` returns a plain `bool`, not a `TypeGuard`, so basedpyright can't use it to narrow `filter_pattern`. Before this change, `if not filter_pattern: return False` narrowed the type to `FilterPattern`. Now `filter_pattern` is still `FilterPattern | None` at `filter_pattern.includes` / `.excludes` on lines 62–74. `pyproject.toml` sets `reportOptionalMemberAccess = "error"`, and the baseline (`.basedpyright/baseline.json`) has no entries of that kind for `filters.py`, so these become new errors and `make static-checks` fails in CI. The runtime behaviour is correct. The fix is to keep an explicit `None` check in the same condition, or to type `filter_pattern_enabled` as `TypeGuard[FilterPattern]`. ✅ Fixed by `@pcbeingused333` in 8baca23 Reply for a change | Was this helpful? Entities without a name are now kept when the filter pattern has no includes or excludes, fixing Superset dashboards being silently filtered out under "scan all" patterns. The basedpyright CI failure from dropping the `if not filter_pattern` guard was resolved by keeping the explicit None check in `_filter`.
